author: NorthEast News Desk
body: LIV Golf received interim court approval to access $14 million in bankruptcy financing, giving the professional golf circuit near-term cash to continue operations during its Chapter 11 restructuring.

A federal bankruptcy judge in New Jersey approved the company’s first-day motions, including authority to pay wages, benefits and critical vendors. The interim amount is part of a proposed $49.6 million debtor-in-possession financing package backed by BC Partners Credit.

LIV filed for bankruptcy Tuesday after financial pressures left players and other creditors owed millions of dollars, according to court documents cited by Reuters. Chapter 11 allows a company to keep operating while it negotiates a plan to reorganize debts under court supervision.

The judge’s order is temporary and does not approve the full financing package or a final restructuring plan. A hearing on broader financing authority is scheduled for October 7. LIV has said it hopes to emerge from bankruptcy in early 2027, but that timeline will depend on creditor negotiations, court approval and the company’s ability to fund ongoing tournaments.
dek: A New Jersey court approved first-day Chapter 11 relief that lets the golf circuit continue paying employees and vendors while it reorganizes.
headline: LIV Golf wins interim access to $14 million in bankruptcy financing
